newsitem.title: JAPAN: Furukawa, others agree on Australia copper venture.
newsitem.headline: Furukawa, others agree on Australia copper venture.

text.p: Furukawa Co Ltd said on Monday that it and four other firms, including one Australian company, had agreed to form a copper smelting venture in New South Wales, Australia.
The other firms include Nissho Iwai Corp, Itochu Corp and Nittetsu Mining Co Ltd, Furukawa and the three Japanese companies said in a joint statement.
The statement did not name the Australian partner.
It said the venture, to be called Port Kembla Copper Pty Ltd (PKC), would buy a copper smelting plant in Port Kembla, Wollongong, currently owned by Southern Copper Ltd, the statement said.
Southern Copper is a wholly owned subsidiary of Anglo-Australian mining giant RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd.
PKC will be 50 percent owned by Furukawa, 20 percent by Nittetsu, 17.5 percent by Nissho Iwai and 10 percent by Itochu, the statement said.
The venture will renovate the plant so it can meet pollution regulations and boost its copper production capacity to 120,000 tonnes a year from 80,000 tonnes currently, the statement said.
The plant stopped operations at the end of 1994 as it needed funds to meet the regulations.
Investment for the renovation and capacity increase is expected to total about A$250 million, the statement said.
Operations at the plant are expected to begin in the second half of 1998, it said.
The venture is considering further boosting the plant's capacity to 150,000 tonnes a year and aiming to boost sales in Asia as well as Australia, the statement said.
